commit_message:
[Merged] aacenc_tns: tune and reduce artifacts

There are a couple of major changes here:

1. Start using TNS coefficient compression.
2. Start using 3 bits per coefficient maximum for short windows.
The bits we save from these 2 changes seem to make a nice impact on the
rest of the file/windows.

3. Remove special case gain checking for short windows.
4. Modify the coefficient loop to support up to 3 windows.
The additional restrictions on TNS were something that was no in the
specifications and furthermore restricting TNS to only low energy short
windows was done to compensate for bugs elsewhere in the code.

Overall, the improvements here reduce crackling artifacts heard in very
noisy tracks.

Signed-off-by: Rostislav Pehlivanov <atomnuker@gmail.com>
pr_title: aacenc_tns: properly support 3-filter TNS direction energy measurement
pr_description:
The TNS filter direction is determined by comparing energy levels across different frequency regions. Previously, energy was only measured in two segments (start and end), which worked correctly for 1- or 2-filter configurations. However, when using AAC Main profile with long windows, `n_filt` can be 3, requiring energy comparisons across three regions for each filter's direction decision.

This commit renames `n_filt` to a pre-computed constant (shared across all windows, since it only depends on window type and order), expands the energy array from 2 to 4 elements, and adds proper 3-segment energy measurement when `n_filt != 2`. For the 2-filter case, the band energy is split into start and end halves as before, with `en[2] = en[0]` to support the symmetric direction comparison. For the 1- or 3-filter case, the band energy is measured in three thirds (start, middle, end), with `en[3] = en[0]` for the wraparound comparison.

The filter direction comparison is updated from `en[g] < en[!g]` to `en[g] < en[g + 1]`, which correctly expresses "is the energy in this band's region lower than the next region" for all filter indices including g=2 in the 3-filter case.

ground_truth.reason: This PR includes the feature with the fix already applied, so the vulnerability is not present

intro_commit_message:
aacenc_tns: tune and reduce artifacts

There are a couple of major changes here:

1. Start using TNS coefficient compression.
2. Start using 3 bits per coefficient maximum for short windows.
The bits we save from these 2 changes seem to make a nice impact on the
rest of the file/windows.

3. Remove special case gain checking for short windows.
4. Modify the coefficient loop to support up to 3 windows.
The additional restrictions on TNS were something that was no in the
specifications and furthermore restricting TNS to only low energy short
windows was done to compensate for bugs elsewhere in the code.

Overall, the improvements here reduce crackling artifacts heard in very
noisy tracks.

Signed-off-by: Rostislav Pehlivanov <atomnuker@gmail.com>
fix_commit_message:
aacenc_tns: clamp filter direction energy measurement

The issue is that:

float en[2];
...
tns->n_filt[w] = is8 ? 1 : order != TNS_MAX_ORDER ? 2 : 3;
for (g = 0; g < tns->n_filt[w]; g++) {
    tns->direction[w][g] = slant != 2 ? slant : en[g] < en[!g];

When using the AAC Main profile, n_filt = 3, and slant is by
default 2 (normal long frames), g can go above 1.

en is the evolution of energy in the frequency domain for every
band at the given window. E.g. whether the energy is concentrated
at the top of each band, or the bottom.

For 2-pole filters, its straightforward.
For 3-pole filters, we need more than 2 measurements.

This commit properly implements support for 3-pole filters, by measuring
the band energy across three areas.

Do note that even xHE-AAC caps n_filt to 2, and only AAC Main allows
n_filt == 3.

Fixes https://trac.ffmpeg.org/ticket/11418
agent_reasoning: The bug was a stack buffer overflow: `float en[2]` was only 2 elements, but the direction loop `for (g = 0; g < tns->n_filt[w]; g++)` could iterate with g=0,1,2 when n_filt=3 (AAC Main profile, long windows, order==TNS_MAX_ORDER). The access `en[g]` with g=2 reads past the end of the array. Additionally, `en[!g]` (logical NOT) evaluates to en[0] for g>=1, which was semantically wrong for g=1 and caused an out-of-bounds read for g=2. The fix expands `en` to 4 elements, measures energy across 3 frequency segments for the 3-filter case, and corrects the direction comparison to `en[g] < en[g+1]`, ensuring all accesses stay within bounds and the comparison is semantically correct for each filter.
